note: The LLM catalog: which providers the proxy routes to and which models it serves. Source of truth for routing (code-side by owner decision, reviewed in Git, changes at deploy cadence). Read by the Go proxy (embedded at build) and by the Deno api/admin (shared/catalog.ts). Prices here are the FALLBACK list: ingest prices with llm.model_prices when a model has a row (ADR 0003). auth_style: x-api-key (Anthropic native), bearer (OpenAI-compatible), both. allowed_paths are regexes on the caller's path after /llm/<provider>; anything else is refused so a caller can't pivot into org/admin endpoints. Cache rates absent => 0.1x / 1.25x input. long_context: past above_prompt_tokens (fresh + cache read + cache write) the WHOLE request bills at the tier rates. per_request_cost_usd: flat charge per call; such models get a usage row for every 2xx even without token usage. upstream_model_slug: the slug sent upstream when it differs from the client-facing one (ADR 0002). request_overrides: shallow merge into JSON request bodies, never for model. To add a model: edit this file, set the provider key in Doppler, release.

openai.note: OpenAI native. Also serves speech-to-text (/v1/audio/transcriptions, multipart audio): the proxy reads the form's model field for authorization, then forwards the bytes unchanged.

cortecs.note: Cortecs (cortecs.ai): EU-only inference aggregator, OpenAI-compatible. All routed providers (tensorix, scaleway, inceptron, berget) run in the EU, which is why the GLM / MiniMax slugs live here. OpenCode Zen was dropped on 2026-09-09: its /zen/go endpoint became coding-agent-only (400 MissingSessionID without an opencode/pi session).

tensorx.note: Tensorx (tensorx.ai): EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible, a LiteLLM-style router. Namespaces its model ids with a vendor prefix (z-ai/glm-5.3, moonshotai/kimi-k2.6); the bare slug 403s. No header picks a backend. Reached only through the <slug>@tensorx variants, which set upstream_model_slug to the namespaced id (ADR 0002).

google.note: Google Gemini API through its OpenAI-compatible layer at /v1beta/openai/chat/completions rather than /v1/chat/completions, hence strip_path_prefix. NOT an EU-residency provider: the Gemini API gives no region guarantee (Vertex AI would), so this is for our own use and experiments, not a default for customer text.

jev.note: Jev: TypeSafe System One, a calibrated classifier API, not a chat model. Callers POST /llm/jev/v1/systemone with Jev's own body ({model, state, questions}); the response comes back unchanged. Not in the pi catalog (it speaks no chat protocol).

jev-images.note: Jev with image input. Jev 1.13+ reads images (base64 in a top-level assets map, or multipart parts) only when the request carries TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true; TypeSafe calls image input experimental. A separate route with its own -images model slugs so production jev callers never send that header and image usage shows up separately in the ledger. Same upstream, key and price as jev. A provider with upstream_headers only serves its own model slugs (the proxy enforces it).

claude-opus-5-5.note: Anthropic cache rates from platform.claude.com pricing: reads at 0.1x input (0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5), 5-minute writes at 1.25x. (1-hour writes are 2x; nothing requests the 1h TTL, if that changes the write rates must change.) The 5.5 generation verbatim from platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (read 2026-10-13). Opus/Sonnet 5.5 bill the full 1M context at the base rate.

claude-haiku-5-5.note: Priced by prompt length: base rates up to 100,000 prompt tokens, 5x above that (long_context).

gpt-5.6-sol.note: OpenAI prices from developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (read 2026-08-20), Standard tier. Explicit cached-input rate (0.1x input on gpt-5.6, 0.25x on o3) used verbatim for cache reads. Cache writes are surcharged on gpt-5.6 at 1.25x input; o3 lists no write rate, so write = 1.0x input. Deliberately a tight set: the three gpt-5.6 tiers, gpt-6-luna, o3, and the two token-billed transcription models.

gpt-6-luna.note: Same pricing page, read 2026-10-15. Short context (up to 272K input) 0.10 / cached 0.01 / write 0.125 / output 0.50; long context (>272K) 0.20 / 0.02 / 0.25 / 0.75.

gpt-4o-transcribe.note: Transcription (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions, multipart), pricing page read 2026-10-13. One input and one output rate; usage.input_tokens (audio + prompt text) is all billed at the input rate. Cache rates equal input only to stop the 0.1x/1.25x fallback; the API never reports cache tokens. whisper-1 is deliberately absent: billed per minute, usage {type: duration} carries no tokens, so it passes through unpriced.

kimi-k3.note: kimi-k3 and kimi-k2.7-code are routed via cortecs (EU-only), not native Moonshot. Cortecs EUR rates (k3: 2.693 in / 13.464 out, k2.7-code: 0.673 in / 3.142 out, cache read 0.18) converted at ~1.1 USD/EUR. Cortecs lists no cache pricing for k3, so its cache rates are the assumed defaults. Native Moonshot rows: published cache-miss input / output rates from platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing; cache rates ASSUMED (read 0.1x, write 1.0x input) until verified.

deepseek-chat.note: deepseek-chat / deepseek-reasoner are the legacy aliases of deepseek-v4-flash (retired 2026-07-24), priced at the v4-flash rate they aliased. DeepSeek bills cache hits at ~0.1x the miss rate and does not surcharge writes (read 0.1x, write 1.0x input); its usage block reports hits as prompt_cache_hit_tokens.

deepseek-v4-pro.note: Served natively by api.deepseek.com (verified 2026-08-10). deepseek-v4-flash retired 2026-10-09, replaced by deepseek-v4.1-flash on cortecs.

gemini-3.8-flash.note: Prices from ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (read 2026-09-28), paid tier, Standard, prompts <= 200k. Output includes thinking tokens, which the usage block reports only as the gap between total_tokens and prompt + completion. No cache-write surcharge. gemini-3.8-flash is on an introductory price through 2026-12-31 and DOUBLES on 2027-01-01 (1.50 / 7.50 / 0.15): update then.

gemini-3.1-flash-lite.note: The cheap tier. 3.1 Flash-Lite did a Finnish polish as well as 3.8 Flash in 1.2 s against 2.8 s (2026-09-28). Lite models have no introductory price.

qwen3.8-27b.note: Cortecs slugs are Cortecs' own (GET api.cortecs.ai/v1/models). Prices are their EUR/Mtok converted at 1 EUR = 1.1554 USD (2026-08-10). Newer entries use the published per-model cache_read_cost; no cache-WRITE rate is published, so writes = 1.0x input. Older GLM / MiniMax rows keep a 0.1x read assumption until reverified. qwen3.8-27b (compact, multimodal) and qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b (flagship MoE) are reasoning models; reasoning tokens ride inside completion_tokens.

glm-5.3.note: GLM 5.3 family routes through cortecs, which fronts tensorix (and berget) and accepts the bare slugs, so no upstream_model_slug. Thinking model: reasoning tokens ride inside completion_tokens. The flash variant is multimodal. The tensorx-native route is glm-5.3@tensorx. (Moved from opencode-zen 2026-08-31.)

deepseek-v4.1-flash.note: Added 2026-10-09, replaces native deepseek-v4-flash. Reasoning + tools + image input, 1M context. Only tensorix returns structured tool_calls: aki (cortecs' default) leaks raw DSML markup into content, which breaks every agent loop. Hence the provider pin. Cortecs does not treat allowed_providers as strict, so a tensorix outage would silently degrade tools. reasoning_effort none really disables thinking here (unlike GLM).

kimi-k2.6@cortecs.note: Provider-pinned variants (<slug>@<provider>, ADR 0002). The bare slug is the platform-routed default; @provider pins one. Each variant is its own entry: authz, pricing and usage_log.model key on the full slug. Only providers that serve the model and publish a price get a variant. Every variant must set upstream_model_slug, even to the bare slug, or the provider 404s. @cortecs: EUR/Mtok from cortecs GET /v1/models at 1.1554 USD/EUR; cache write = input.

kimi-k3@tensorx.note: @tensorx: USD/token from tensorx GET /v1/model/info (2026-09-23) x 1e6; cache write = input (tensorx publishes none).

jev-latest.note: TypeSafe docs (Models page, 2026-10-16): $0.042 per million input tokens, output free, no per-request charge; same for every version and long context. per_request_cost_usd stays 0 only so a call is still logged per key if a response lacks usage. Aliases move between versions (jev-latest -> jev-1.13.0, jev-preview -> jev-1.14.0), so versioned ids are listed too.

jev-latest-images.note: Image-enabled twins for the jev-images route: jev-latest-images is upstream jev-latest, and so on. Priced like their base slugs.
